examples.trans: I am an adult and I decide everything myself.

examples.text: Сами решайте, что делать.
examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Мы вместе решаем все вопросы.
examples.trans: We decide all matters together.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Вика, а ты не могла бы добавить?
examples.trans: Vika, could you chip in a little?

examples.text: Кто меня вообще может уволить с работы?
examples.trans: Who could ever fire me from work?

examples.text: Могу я тоже отплатить тебе добром?
examples.trans: Can I also repay you with kindness?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('would') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вика, а ты не могла бы добавить?
examples.trans: Vika, could you chip in a little?

examples.text: Да, хотя бы сказать эту простую правду.
examples.trans: Yes, at least tell that simple truth.

examples.text: Я бы подумал.
examples.trans: I would think about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (root 'бавить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to add', forming an aspectual pair with 'добавлять'.

examples.text: Вика, а ты не могла бы добавить?
examples.trans: Vika, could you chip in a little?

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'otherwise', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: We were starting to worry, you see.

examples.text: Быстрее, а то опоздаем.
examples.trans: Faster, or we'll be late.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a little'.

examples.text: Поработать немного надо.
examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Я немного устал.
examples.trans: I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'money', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: А то мне немного денег не хватает.
examples.trans: Otherwise I do not have quite enough money.

examples.text: Вика, держи, вот деньги за моё ружьё.
examples.trans: Vika, take this, here is the money for my rifle.

examples.text: Чтобы тебе вернули за него мои деньги?
examples.trans: So that they would refund my money for it to you?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to grab', forming an aspectual pair with 'схватить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: А то мне немного денег не хватает.
examples.trans: Otherwise I do not have quite enough money.

examples.text: Почему он меня хватает?
examples.trans: Why is he grabbing me?

examples.text: Не хватай меня!
examples.trans: Don't grab me!
